My advice would be to start with the main albums, white album, sergeant pepper, revolver, magical mystery and the like.

I would suggest that you focus on the albums released to a specific country (ie only American or British) to eliminate needless repetition. And build your collection from there. Don't worry about the singles as you'll already have those songs on the full albums.

Hope this helps.

Btw are you looking for physical copies or electronic?

>What about songs released on singles that aren't on albums

All their singles (some of which aren't on the 12 main albums) are on Past Masters, but I think that includes some overlap with the albums.

Coming at this from another angle, try to get the mono versions instead of the stereo ones. Almost all of their work was recorded in mono originally and later remastered in stereo (the big exceptions being Let It Be and Abby Road). This isn't about hearing the original versions or some elitist audiophile thing, most of the stereo mixes are just pretty damn awful.
